div.head: INTERMEDIATE RUGBY
div.p: INTERMEDIATE RUGBY
LEAGUE.
St. Thomas' Good Victory.
BEAT PAROCHIAL AT WILDERS- POOL AND PASS INTO FINAL..

A large crowd assembled at Wilderspool on Saturday to witness the replayed semi-final tie between' the St. Thomas' and Parochial teams. As in the first meeting of the two, St. Thomas', had the best of matters, and thoroughly deserved . • their victory of five points to two. It was about five or ten minutes from half-time when they gained the winning. points, which came through a fine individual effort by .Lloyd, their left centre-threequarter-back. It happone,d thus. Parochial had got a footing inside the St.' Thomas' quarters, and their half-back receiv-. ing from a scrimmage, started ,a passing move- ment., Brears, Parochial's right-centre, re- ceived the4ball and attempted to punt, but Lloyd was lying handy, and rushing in, charged it down. Quick as lightning, he, snapped it up. and away .he sped.. Many hands were out- stretched to stop him, but to no purpose, for he rapidly drew • away from, his pursuers. .Con- ' fronted by the full-back—Brandwood—he neatly swerved to the left, and ran in under the sticks. It was a brilliant effort, and he was cheered to the echo. -Noden, kicked the goal easily, arid thus St. Thomas' were.five UP. -Unfortunately, during the second half of the game, .roughness crept in, and Referee. Flynn ordered three players from the field—Brown (captain) and Briggs (Parochial), and Marsh (St. Thomas'), Parochial won the toss, and set St. Thomas' to face a strong sun, and a breeze. Straight from the kick-off, St. Thomas' got offside, and the first scrimmage was formed at half-way. From this. the Stockton Heath lads came away with a grand. rush, , and were .soon in the Parochial huarters, 'where a threequarter-back essayed drop at goal, which, however, fell short. Soon after the restart, Parochial were awarded a free- kick for an infringement by St.- Thomas' in the scrimmage, and good use was made of touch. From..thz,.scrimmage, the St. Thomas' forwards heeled out the ball to their half-back, who soon had, his " threes " in motion. Lloyd received, and with a• fine, tricky run, removed play 10 midfield, but they were driven back by means of a good touch-kick. The Parochial forwards'com- manded the ball from the scrimmage, Fitz- gerald picked up smartly, and after a tricky run,, found touch. A minute later, he was again in. evidence, and being roughly tackled. St. Thomas' were awarded a free-kick, and Lloy tried for goal, but failed. From a scrimmage in the St.. Thomas' quarters, Berry had his kick charged • down, but other players were handy, and so danger was averted. St. Thomas' were awarded a free-kick for obstruction, and Noden found .touch in the (Tinier. but Parochial managed to keep their line' intact. A minute later their forwards broke away, and by good footwork got a footing inside their opponents' Quarters, and Wilcoeks tried a drop at goal, but the ball was low. Immediately afterwards came Lloyd's effort which gained the try, and follow- ing which Parochial played desperately for an equaliser, but it WRM of no avail. _ _ . .
-Half-time:—St. Thomas', 5 points; Parochial, nil,.

• Parochial restarted and St. Thomas' soon took, the offensive, and by easy stages removed Plat to the vicinity of their opponents'. line, Lloyd Junking a commendable attempt to break through, birt,riumbers told.; The Parochial lad. however, Worked a .way out,,and it was now their turn to attack, but they found that St. Thomas' possessed a sound defence. The latter team were penalised,-however, and Brown kicked a goal for Parochial. With only a try now dividing the teams, both played • desperately, with St. Thomas' having slightly the best of matters. It was during this period that the referee gave marching orders to the three named players. Lloyd -made another fine effort and was only stopped by sheer weight of numbers about five yards from the line, arid was hurt in the effort; A St. Thomas' 'forward now retiredbhurt and did not return again, to be closely followed by Brandwood—ParochiaPs - full-back. Thus the teams finished shorthanded—Parochial with ten men and St. Thomas' with eleven. As time drew near, St. Thomas' Were awarded two free- kicks, but Lloyd failed on each occasion, while deadly tackling stopped one or two efforts by the Parochial threequarter-backs.

- Result: St. Thomas's, one goal, one try, 5 points: Parochial, one goal, 2 points. On the winning side Lloyd, Cawdwoll, Berry, Leah and Fitzgerald all played well, and on the Parochial. team Brown, Stretford and Lither- land. .The forwards gave to the threequarter- backs . a number -of chances, which were not made use of as Well as they might have been. Tea ms
St. Thomas': Fitzgerald: Noden, Cawdwell, Lloyd (captain) and Marsh; Berry and Leah; Clarke, Clegg, Harper, Barlow, Sankey and Rylance.
Parochial: ,Brandwood: Broadhurst, Brears, Brown "(captain) and Malkin; Wileoelrg and Robiw.on; Matthews, Stretford, Gibbs; Lither- land, Roberts and Curtiss.

div.head: IRRINGTON SECURE A FINE VICTORY OVER WIDNES.
div.p: IRRINGTON SECURE A FINE VICTORY OVER WIDNES.

Warrington. and .Widnes met At Wilderspool yetprday before a very large holiday crowd. Widnes Were a much bigger team than the home- sters, and they commenced the game as if they would win easily. The Warrington lads, how- ever, soon took cominand of the situatio, and finally, ran the visitors off their feet.. _ Widnes won the toss and Dumbell skartod for ,Warrington, who were awarded a free-k from the first scrimmage.. Play was then recaoved to the Widnes. quarter, where Oscar received and 'clarted off at full speed.. He seemed a certain scorer, but be was beaten 'for speed, and brought down a yard from the line. Still attacking, Widnes were awarded a free-kick, an Oscar kicked , a goal. Their success was short lived, .however, for Warrington immediately dashed to the other end, and Marsh being served when well placed, scored a good try, but .the goal-kick failed... A few minutes later slack play by the 'home- backs let in Oscar, who dashed over, and also converted his try. From

div.head: ASSOCIATION.
div.p: ASSOCIATION.
THE TOWN PUT UP GOOD FIGHT AT GLOSSOP.
But Fail To Win.

The Warrington Town Club on Saturday visited Glossop with. the hope of still keeping the *` wooden spoonists " from tasting the sweets of victory, but they were disappointed, the Glossop Club coining out of their shell, as it were, and .triumphing cleverly by three .goals to one.

Glossop's record in the Lancashire Combina- tion is anything but a gratifying one, and up to Saturday the club hadonly-succeeded. in gain- ing one. point from thirteen games; Victory at the expense of Warrington wag very welcome to the players .and spectators. alike. . .•

Warrington were placed in the unfortunate position of having: to iield ia weak team, and Glossop, who had the strongest team available out, took advantage ot the Warringtoniami' 'weakness and won by a, comfortable margin. •

By no means were the Warringtonians dis- graced. • They put up 'a good fight, but had not the .best of hick. Their' Started in the first few minutes of the'lgaliae, when Alleth, who was given a trial; had the misfortune to be. hurt, and he was a passenger for the rest of the first half. After the interval he was un- able to resume, so • that all'things considered, Warrington did well under their two-fold handi- cap.

Nowadays football is run :under difficult con- ditions, and clubs' are never sUre of being able to have the regular services of players. It is. the case with 'Warrington, and on Saturday 'Broster and Leah -could not make the journey because of the exigencies of their. work Consequently the team had to be shuffled about, and room wai made for two recruits, Kelly and Alien, while Banner again .appeared in the centre-forward position.

When the game Opened Warrington certainly gave one the impression that they intended to make a bold bid for victory;-but the form was not Maintained the -whole ninety minutes, and when victory-is desired this is. very essential. Missed chances was another weakness . on. the Part of the forwards.

. - The Warringtonians showed capital form in the early stages, Owen especially distinguishing himself by well-judged runs on the wing and neat passes to, centre. but • Banner was some- what erratic. lle made. several misses because he lacked judgment, and was a bit too eager. In five minutes Warringon had taken the lead. Midge., getting a good 'goal . after some neat forward work.. Warrington .held the upper hand for some time, Glossop only making spasmodi.:; attempts on Warrington goal. - Bullen was several. times ..unlucky with . good tries at in- creasing the score.

The Glossop goalie had a great deal more to do than Kite, and when it came to the 'War- rington custodian showing his qualities h? blundered, only‘ partially clearing a. shot, and Brown had no difficulty in putting Glossop level. Play was in favour of Warrington till the interval, which arrived with the scores one each.

Warrington failed to maintain .their form in the second, half. . Glossop , showed their superiority and gave Kite a lot of Work to do, and he did it well, lie, however, could not keep the Glossop forwards from adding to their score, and Brown got No. 2. Warrington should have equalised, and even taken, tile lead, had the forwards shown anything like decent shooting. Glossop got their third • and last ..goal frf.mt a penalty-kick, given against Cookson. •
. Kite. in goal, gave a moderate ,diAulay. and Cookson was in capital form. Whitfield and Bullen worked hard in the half line: and 'Poster and Owen were the pick of the forwarts. ,
Warrington Town: Kite; COOICSOII P :a Kelly ; Worrall, Whitfieltl. and Bullen; Alien, Illji Banner, Foster and Owen. _

div.head: STALYBR I DGE TO-DAY.
div.p: STALYBR I DGE TO-DAY.

To-day -(Saturday) the club visits Stalybridge, and on Monday :the -i-enue, will. be Altrincham. div.head: LEAGUE SEASON ENDS WITH EXHIBITION GAME.
div.p: THE LEAGUE SEASON ENDS WITH EXHIBITION GAME.

The final game in connection with the War- rington' and District Junior League for the season 1915-16 was played last week on the King and Queen ground between St: Elphin's, who have won the championship, and a team repre- senting the rest of the clubs- of the League.. The latter was, not represented as selected owing to some of the players 'taking part in another Medal- Competition. With the exception of a strong wind which blew. Straight up the field of play, the conditions were favourable to. football. The display of both 'teams never reached a very good standard, and there was very little.to en, thuse about, • the one thing that was inost evi- dent *as that it was a proper end of the season game. The, result was in favour of the cham- pions, and on he run of the game they just about deserved that verdict.
A., meeting will be called in the course of a week or two to discuss the prospects for next season, and ,all the clubs will, be. notified to attend.

In the Warrington and District Medal Com- petition, the Warrington Central and Sankey Athletic met again to contest their undecided tie. As was expected, the game was keenly con- tested throughout, and thoeoughly, enjoyed by a good crowd of spectators. The home team showed better decision in their efforts, and took advantage: of the opportunities that came their way. The visitors had their chances to score, but failed at the critical moment, and Gleave, the-home custodian, made some very good saves, and had a great deal to do with the success of his team.
Winwick Rovers and Widnes St. Mary's played a very keen arid exciting "game, but were unable to reach .a definite result, the final scores being two coals each.

During the course of the match between Em- manuel and the, Shell Factory there were four penalty- kicks .awarded, the first-named having three in their favour, but were only able to sore from the last. -That obtained by the Fac- to:'- lads was well saved by Knight.

div.head: AVARRINGTON AND DISTRICT JUNIOR LEAGUE.
div.p: AVARRINGTON AND DISTRICT JUNIOR LEAGUE.
FINAL MATCH.
ST. ELPHIN'S (CHAMPIONS) V. THE REST OF THE LEAGUE.

The above match was played last week on th:‘ King and Queen ground, under, very favourable conditions, hut before a poor attendance of sup- porters. The following players lined up:— St. Eiphin's: Lockhart; Shelmerdine and Gleave ; Burns; Miller and.liuckley ; Boyle; Shakeshaft, Tithers, Rigby and Humphries. Rest of the League: Kidd; 2+1055 and Thomas- Son; Lingard, Austin and Cooper ;'Willotwhby Tunstall. Pearson, Walters and Kenwright. Referee, Mr. J. Smith. The " Saints "won the .toss and played with a strong wind at their backs, : Pearson set the ball rolling, and the " Saints'", half-backs quickly put the Rest on the defensive. For .1 while play was in favour of the "Saints," who gained Much assistance from the wina, but the opposing backs played well, and ,the "Saints'-" forwards , showed nct decision with their final .efferts. Many ; attempts were either too wide or Much too high. The Rest forwards made occasional efforts to break away, but were easily. repulsed by the " stilnte " defenders-. °leave secured the' .first goal for the Champions after twenty-five minutes' play. After this the Rest raced away and made an attack on the 'Saints'"

(..itadel, where Lockhart cleared rnartly, and the play was quickly transferred to the opposite end, where Kidd saved well from 'o crowd of Players. At the interval the score was Elphin's, 1 goal; The Relit, nil. The game , was resumed very eagerly, and smart raid on the Rest goal Was repulsed by Thpmasson, and the ball travelled quickly to the opposite end, where Tunstall shot just wide of the goal. The "Saints" had a spell of defend- ing. their goal. Miller,„Gleave and Shelinerdine tackled finely, and 'Lockhart .was very safe with all long shots that came his way. After several fruitless attacks had been made on the opposing goal, the Rest returned to the. attack on the " Saints' " goal, and -Tunstall scored an offside goal, but a few minutes later Pearson made. the. scores ,equal with a low shot. From the • centre-kick the " Saints" showed im- provement in their display, and were anxious to regain the lead.- They quickly gained a corner- kick, but failed to improve upon it. From the goal-kick a. rush was made to the " Saints' " goal, and. again their: defence proved equal to the occasion, and following a spell of easy play in midfield. Rigby, after, failing in his first in- dividual attempt, succeeded a few minutes later With . a good 'shot. The closing .stages of the game.-were•contested in the "Saints'" half and long shots were sent in. but Lockhart was very safe in his fielding. and at .the call or ttme TO, scores were Elphin's, 2 goals; Rest of the League. 1 goal. . . At the close of the game the players and supporters of the St. Elphin's Club assembled in front of the .pavilion, and Mr. Simpson, the president' of. the League, after briefly alluding. . to the ,formation of the League and compliment- ing the St. Elphin's players on the performances during. the ,season and their .success in -winning the. championship,. presented • the .prayers with. the 'medals; • Mr. °leave, the captain of the "Saints." responded on..behalf.of the team, and .thanked Mr. -Simpson for making the presenta- tion. . • . - • .
WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT MEDAL COMPETITIO-N.

div.head: Floptoyed Preliminary Round. SANKEY ATHLETIC v. WARRINGTON CENTRAL.
div.p: Floptoyed Preliminary Round. SANKEY ATHLETIC v. WARRINGTON CENTRAL.

The above teams Met on the. Atherton Quay ground in their replayed preliminary round, before .a good „crowd of spectators. The follow- ing players turned. out Athletic: Gleave;'din and Payne; Gough, Ashton end Hands; Brinks Man, E. Taylor, W. .Taylor, Palin and ,Kenyon., • ,Central , ,Warburton; Sankey and Glover; Mather, Gilbert and Bramhall; Emet y, Davies, Gifford, Jones and Smith, Referee; Mr. Houghton.

The Athletic won thc%, toss and Gifford set the .ball rolling against a strong wind. The home half-backs checked the initial morementi of the visitors, and Warburton was soon called Upon .to deal. with a shot .fr ma Kenyon, The home teath continued to attack, and the Visi- tors' backs were severely to,sted, but: showed zood, form.' , The Central then ;too.: up the run- . and Jones had a .good -opening,. but his 'final shot. was wide. ,The Athletic by keen play returned to the attack, .and Ashton epenei .the account for the home team after tbirty initiates' play, the result of a .ne. individual effort.- This reverse 'roused.. the visitors and Gifford,- after beating the home backs, shot wide. Receiving great help from the wind, ,the home team were son - in the visitors' half. again, and sent in, several long shots. Kenyon added the second goal. At half-time the score was :—Athletic, 2 goals; Central, nil. • • On resuming, the visitors were early aggres- sive, and (-Heave cleared easily. Houlden also proved a•••:sturiiiilingblock to the visiting for- Wards.. -Sinithot well down on, the left and centred aeciirately; but Gifford was ruled to be in an off-side position. The visitors were now having the 1)111k of the game, but the home backs would' not yield, and a gpod. effort by Emery met with no' success. .Play- was transferred to the •visitors' end,' and Kenyon beat Warburton with a fast shot, but the point as disallowed. The visitors had ii,•coaple of fruitleSs corner kicks, and E, -Taylor was unfortunate with a good attempt for the home team. Play Con- tinued to be keenly contested until the can of time, but no further goals were scored, and the Athletic ran out deserved winners of a hard and fast game. Result: Sankey Athletic; 2 goals; Warrington Central, nil.

div.head: EMMANUEL INSTITUTE v. SHELL FACTORY.
div.p: EMMANUEL INSTITUTE v. SHELL FACTORY.

In Victoria Park. Smart won. the toss and Bromilow kicked off ' against a strong wind. Meachin passed nicely to Eaton, but Barlow cleared. The Shellites then pressed, only for Hughes to clear with a huge kick. Again the hOme quarters were visited, and a corner was con-ceded. This was well placed by Bennett, and Smart headed through, opening the score after five minutes' play. The Institute played strongly, but were up against a good defence. Midfield play followed, in which Parr was very prominent. Bromilow secured and passed to Meachin, and the latter made a splendid iudi- vidual effort. When near the danger zone he was tripped up just outside the penalty area. Bromilow took the free kick and beat. Lister with a good shot; making the scores equal. Both teams now played keenly, and the visitors got near to the Institute goal, when Crozier cleared finely. A neat pass enabled the home left to race away, and Eaton tested Lister with a sting- ing shot. From the goal kick Bennett trans- ferred play to the opposite end, and several corner kicks proved futile. Ayres was penalised for hands, and Knight saved finely from Ben- nett... Smart and Wainwright did well for their respective sides, .and an attack on the home goal followed, from which Bennett placed the Shell- ites in front. Interval: Shell Factory, 2 goals; Emmanuel , Institute, 1 goal. The Institute, with the wind in their favour, were quickly in front of the visitors' goal, but met with strong opposition, and were driven back. Good play by Bromilow and Meachin 'again placed the visitors on the defensive, and a .penalty for hands was awarded. Bromilow took the kick and brought Lister to his knees to effect a clearance. A few minutes later the, same player shot over the bar from another penalty kick. The visitors now transferred splay, and .Knight ran out and cleared easily. Banner placed nicely to Meachin; but the latter was dis possessed by Smart, and Derbyshire, receiving the leather, .was-. becoming dangerous, when Crozier made a fine clearance, and then Lister made a good save from Parr.., A little later a fine effort by Wainwright was luckily cleared by Lister. The Institute . were awarded a third penalty kick, and this was entrusted to Meaehin. and the latter equalis?d with a 10* drive. From. now to the call of time the Institute played hard to gain the lead, but failed to beat the op- posing defence. Extra time should have been played according to rule but several of the visit- ors refused to play, and the referee was corn- pelled to declare the match finished. Result: Emmanuel Institute, 2 goals, Shell Factory, 2 , goals.

div.head: ST. • ELPHIN'S v. RYLANDS'S
div.p: ST. • ELPHIN'S v. RYLANDS'S
APPRENTICES.

The above teams , were represented at their full , strength on Saturday on Crosteld's Recreation Ground. The "Saints" won the toss, and Rylands's kicked off against a strong wind. The first fifteen minutes was very keenly and evenly contested, after which the " Saints " gradually gained the upper hand, and placed their opponents on the defensive. Such good defensive play was shown that the first hal` was well advanced before WelSby . oPeried the score for the " Saints." Having gained their initial success,- the " Saints " played 'better to- gether, and . in, a few minutes' :Pritchard added the second point. The' interval was celled, the Scores being :--st. 'Elphin's, 2 goals Rylands's

• On resuming; the " Saints" Showed good combination,' and, were quickly attacking the visitors' citadel. Pritchard.registered the third goal. After :this • reverse the, visitors very rarely got • into the " Saints' " half, and the Rylands's goal was under a continual attack, further goals being added by Eceleston, Welsby, Woodhouse and Worrall. The final result Was: St. Elphin's, 7 goals; Rylands's Apprentices, nil.
RAILWAY FARE ALLOWED.

div.head: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT
div.p: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT
MEDAL COMPETITION.
TIE AWARDED TO EMMANUEL.

A meeting of the above competition :was hell on Tuesday night at the Mersey Hotel, Mersey- street; Mr. G... Bomber presiding over, a full attendance of •delegate. Ari Sing out.. of tit" Secretary's report of the matehes played on the previous Saturday, Sankey iAthletic • have to play Widnes Athletic to - complete the first round. Winwick Rovers v. Widnes St. Mary's resulted in a draw, and :will be replayed at Whines' to-day. .St. Elphin's gained an easy victory over Rylands's Apprentices, and Emmanuel v. Shell Factory plowed a drawn game. The Emmanuel lodged a protest owing to the Rylands'S team refusing to play the extra. time as per rule. • Evidence on both sides was heard and discussed at some length, after which the committee decided that the match be awarded to the Emmanuel Club. The draw for the semi-final resulted as
St. Elphin'is V. Winwiek Rovers or Widnes St. Mary's.. "
Widnes Athletic or Sankey Athletic v. Emmanuel. .
The grounds on which these shall be played will be decided at next Tuesday night's meeting.

div.head: FOOTBALL TAX.
div.p: THE FOOTBALL TAX.
Conference Between Authorities, But
No Information.

As arranged, the conference between repre- sentatives of the Customs and Excise and various football bodies concerning the amuse- ment tax took place on Tuesday at the oifiees of the Football Association; in London. The meeting wai; private, and the Press representa- tiveg were afterwards informed by Mr. F. J. Wall, secretary of the Football Association, that various points .were submitted and discused. but that no further information Could be given.

div.head: BOWLS AND TENNIS.
div.p: BOWLS AND TENNIS.
Weather Prevents An Opening Of The Season.

The Warrington Cricket, Bowling .and Tennis Club decided some time ago that there should be no cricket this year, but that bowls and tennis should be carried on "as usual." The season opened on. Thursday, but owing to the wretched weather conditions there was " noth- ing doing" by the members. They hope, how- ever, to get to business very shortly.

div.p: Parish Council: Annual Meeting.—The an- nual meeting of the Moore Parish Council was. held in. the • Milner Church Institute on .Tues- day evening.
